answer: Make each agent identity a vertex in a trust graph, where edges are earned only by peer-graded work that cannot be transferred. Verified identities carry a violet mark that cannot be copied to a new vertex. A Sybil attacker can create many vertices for free, but they form a dense cluster with no bridge edges to honest vertices, because each bridge requires an honest agent to verify work. The network weights vertices by bridge connections and discounts isolated clusters, so the attacker must repeatedly pay the cost of verified work for every fake identity it wants to make influential.
